text:
sre-bot: ALERT p99 latency breach in us-west-dedicated pool for route /v1/generate — 3m ago, threshold 350ms, observed p99=1287ms :rotating_light:

sre-bot: linked traces: https://internal-traces/redwood/trace/2031122334

maria: saw the alert. any obvious noisy customers?

aj: quick lookup — traffic looks normal. 95th ~= 240ms, but p99 jump tied to a small subset of sessions (~0.7%).

kevin: i pulled a few flamegraphs from profiler-bot — attaching snippet:
```
flamegraph top:
- aten::matmul 42% (kernel: fp16_fused_wide)
- runtime::kv_read 18% (misses spike)
- runtime::microbatcher.wait 12%
- tool_runner::invoke 9% (reentrant)
- scheduler::kernel_select 6% (fallback path)
```

kevin: note the matmul is the wide kernel; it gets selected when seq_len>1024 or when batch concatenation path triggers. these sessions show sequence-length jumps mid-gen.

anita: mid-gen jumps? looks like tool-calls are appending extra markup, then model re-enters longer decoding. we saw something similar with the external-tool loop last quarter.

leo: i just replayed one trace. pattern is: request arrives (len=480), during generation the model emits a tool call token -> runtime pauses to run tool callback -> callback returns appended content (~800 tokens) -> runtime continues generation with new longer context. that pushes kernel selector to wide path, cache misses spike because KV cache wasn't prepared for sudden long prefixes.

aj: that explains microbatcher.wait too — when a single session suddenly expands, the batcher tries to include it and stalls the microbatch for re-ordering. p95 unaffected because majority short; p99 dominated by these reentrant tool sessions.

maria: can we mitigate quickly? fallback kernel that is stable for mixed lengths? or force eviction policy to keep KV warm for that session?

kevin: short-term options:
- cap post-tool appended length at runtime (reject/trim tool output)
- change kernel selector to prefer low-latency kernel for first N tokens after a tool callback (cheap)
- prewarm KV on tool callback completion (async warm)
- microbatcher: don't wait for expanded sessions, push them to slow-path queue to avoid stalling short requests

anita: i like push-to-slow-path. low-risk and quick. patch to microbatcher to classify session as "expanded" and route to dedicated slow lane.

profiler-bot: recent KV metrics for affected host h12:
```
kv_reads: 12k/min (baseline 3.2k)
kv_misses: 9.1k/min (baseline 0.4k)
avg_kv_lookup_ms: 1.9ms -> 11.6ms during incidents
```

leo: also noticed kernel_select calls spike in latency when batch shapes are heterogeneous. selector does a compatibility fallback that incurs compile/copy overhead. that shows up as short-lived 50-200ms hits per request.

maria: ok immediate playbook:
1) enable microbatcher slow-path for expanded sessions (kevin)  — safety toggle to roll back
2) add heuristic: after tool callback, tag session and prefer low-latency kernel for next 256 tokens (kevin)
3) async KV prewarm on tool callback return (anita)
4) run a targeted replay to validate p99 (leo)

kevin: i'll open a tiny PR for 1+2, can ship toggle as runtime flag. aiming for canary in us-west within 2 hours.

anita: i'll add an async prewarm job and a metric to count "expanded" sessions. also add a guard to trim tool outputs > 600 tokens if customer config allows.

leo: i'll run 30m replay sim with synthetic tool callbacks to reproduce spike and measure p95/p99 before/after.

aj: if we do 1+2 we should see p99 collapse. also add a regression eval to catch this in CI (long-toolcall-scenarios).

maria: assigning followups: kevin (microbatcher + kernel-heuristic PR), anita (prewarm + trimming flag), leo (replay + dashboard), aj (CI eval). i'll monitor the canary. :eyes:

kevin: PR link: https://git.redwood/p/runtime/+/1234 — adds slow-path queue + kernel preference flag. very small change.

anita: prewarm draft: https://git.redwood/p/runtime/+/1235 — spawns async kv.touch(seq_hash) after callback returns. also metric: runtime.expanded_sessions_total

leo: replay results (dev canary) after change:
```
baseline p99: 1120ms
post-change p99: 264ms
p95 ~ stable 230->240ms
slow-path traffic: 0.6% of requests
```

maria: nice. schedule postmortem and decide long-term: possibly redesign kernel selector to avoid on-the-fly compiles for shape mismatches and make KV warming part of tool contract.

aj: raising an RFC for tool-calling contract: tool returns should include a "expected_added_tokens" field so runtime can pre-allocate/choose kernels ahead of resume. helps avoid selector thrash.

kevin: noted. will also add in PR a telemetry tag so we can count how many sessions went to slow-path and how many trimmed tool outputs.

maria: great work team — keep the canary running for 4h, then roll to prod if stable. we'll sync in ops standup tomorrow for long-term design. :thumbsup: 

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — p99 back under threshold in us-west after canary rolled. incident duration ~1h20m.
